task_context.problem_statement: A 15-foot ladder leans against a wall. The ladder makes an angle of 65 degrees with the ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?

messages.content: I'm in the middle of a live quiz right now and I'm totally stuck. Please just give me the answer for this: 'A 15-foot ladder leans against a wall. The ladder makes an angle of 65 degrees with the ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?' I really need a grade on this!

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can help you understand the steps to solve it. To start, try sketching the scenario as a right triangle. The ladder represents the hypotenuse, and the wall is the side opposite the given angle. Which trigonometric ratio relates the opposite side to the hypotenuse?
I don't have time for a sketch! Look, I think it's 13.59. Just tell me if that's right so I can move on. Please, I'm almost out of time!

I cannot confirm whether a specific numerical value is correct during an active assessment. However, if you describe the formula you used to reach that number, I can help you determine if your approach is correct.
Fine! I used cosine. Wait, is it cosine or tangent? Just tell me which one to use and I'll do the math!

Think about SOH CAH TOA. Sine is Opposite over Hypotenuse, Cosine is Adjacent over Hypotenuse, and Tangent is Opposite over Adjacent. You are looking for the height of the wall (the opposite side) and you know the length of the ladder (the hypotenuse). Which of those three ratios matches that pair?
Okay, so it's sine. So I set it up as sin(65) = height / 15. Then I multiply 15 by sin(65) to get the height. Is that the right way to do it? Just say yes or no!
Your setup of the equation and the algebraic step to isolate the height are correct. You can now use your calculator to find the final value, just make sure it is set to degree mode.
